name: Web front end
signal: HTML, CSS, browser code

scope.not_when: the screen is a native mobile app, or the change is server-only

obligations.what: CRA reporting applies where the front end is part of a product with digital elements (`aidd-team:incident-response`), and the main obligations from 2027-12-11. A website that supports no product's function is out of scope (Recital 12).
Beside the CRA, the EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: software placed on the market after this date is a product, and a missing update can make it defective.

checklist.item: Name the pages, components, and states the change touches; a user-facing change needs the product designer and `design.files`. A front end that is part of a product with digital elements is in CRA scope. A site that sells to EU consumers, or offers banking, e-books, or passenger transport, meets the European Accessibility Act, which builds on WCAG.
Acceptance names every state per screen (empty, loading, error, partial, success, offline) and the keyboard path through it.
The browser support target is Baseline Widely available (or a named Baseline year) in the Spec; a feature outside it has a fallback.

No non-essential cookie, storage, or tracker runs before consent where ePrivacy Art. 5(3) applies. A Global Privacy Control signal is an opt-out where a US state law requires it, as California, Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, and others do.

Rendering per route: static or server-rendered by default, client-rendered only for an app-like screen; the Spec names the JavaScript each route hydrates. Server data lives in one query cache with its staleness (`aidd-team:caching`), and UI state stays local or in the URL.
Semantic HTML first, ARIA only where HTML has no element; focus order and a visible focus ring preserved.

No inline script and no `unsafe-inline`: nonces or hashes under the CSP. Every third-party script is named in the Spec and pinned with `integrity` (SRI), or self-hosted when its bytes change by design. A `Permissions-Policy` turns off the features the page does not use.
Session cookies are `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`, with the `__Host-` prefix. A state-changing request checks a CSRF token or the `Origin` header.

Untrusted strings reach the DOM only through escaping or a sanitizer, with Trusted Types enforced (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) where the engines support it; URLs are validated before `href` or `src`.
Animate `transform` and `opacity` where you can: a layout property shifts the layout (CLS) and costs a frame. Motion has a reduced alternative (`prefers-reduced-motion`).
Core Web Vitals field data and the client error rate are the observe signals.

name: APIs and services
signal: HTTP, gRPC, events, webhooks

scope.not_when: the interface stays inside one process, such as an internal function signature

checklist.item: A changed request, response, status code, event, GraphQL type, or Protobuf message is a contract change: never minor.

The OpenAPI or AsyncAPI change, the GraphQL schema, or the `.proto` file is written before Spec approval and listed in `design.files`, so Spec approval freezes it. The Acceptance references its operations and schemas.
Errors, idempotency, and versioning follow `aidd-team:api-design`. Rate limits, quotas, and spending limits on paid providers are stated (OWASP API4).

Validate input against the contract at the boundary. Authorize per object and per property (OWASP API1, API3). Paginate every list. A GraphQL server caps depth and cost and takes only persisted operations from first-party clients.

Webhooks are signed and carry an id and a timestamp; a receiver verifies them and drops a replay (Standard Webhooks). A sender resolves each target URL and refuses private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses, after each redirect too (OWASP API7).

Real time: server-sent events for server-to-client updates, WebSocket only for two-way traffic. Each connection authenticates when it opens, sends heartbeats, bounds its send buffer, and resumes after a drop (SSE's `Last-Event-ID`, or a sequence number); fan-out across instances goes through a pub/sub channel.

Tokens follow RFC 9700: no implicit or password grant, PKCE, exact redirect URIs, and short-lived or sender-constrained tokens. API keys are stored hashed, shown once, scoped, expiring, and prefixed so a secret scanner finds a leak.
Only additive changes without a version bump. A removal follows `aidd-team:api-design`'s expand and contract and is recorded in the Spec's `deprecations`, so a passed sunset warns.
Consumer contract tests pass for every known consumer before rollout. 4xx and 5xx rates and p95 latency are the observe signals; calls to deprecated operations are counted per consumer.

tests.proves: the `.proto` files lint clean and break no wire or JSON compatibility
tests.how: `buf lint` and `buf breaking --against '.git#branch=<base>'` (buf v1.73.0), with `when_changed` on the `.proto` files

tests.proves: no high finding on the changed operations
tests.how: `zap-api-scan.py` from the ZAP 2.17.0 image against a test deployment

tests.name: Load test
tests.proves: the SLO holds under expected load
tests.how: the load-test runner's `tests` entry, such as `k6 run`, with the SLO as thresholds that fail the run

name: Mobile apps
signal: iOS, Android, cross-platform

scope.not_when: the change is a mobile-web page (`aidd-team:web-front-end`) or a desktop app (`aidd-team:desktop-apps`)

checklist.item: A store-facing change (permissions, data, SDKs, payments, sign-in, accounts, children) is major. Store review is a dependency, and the build meets the stores' dated minimums.
Each permission with its purpose string and, for a Play restricted permission, its Play Console declaration. The privacy manifest, App Privacy, and Data safety changes as Tasks.

Digital goods through in-app purchase (3.1.1) and Play Billing; any other payment names its exception (3.1.3, physical goods, a Play exemption, or a storefront's own rule in the US, the EU, or Japan).
Account creation brings in-app deletion (5.1.1(v)) and, on Play, a web link that deletes without the app. A social login brings an equivalent private login (4.8).
User-generated content has filtering, reporting, blocking, and published contact (1.2); an app for children follows the Kids Category (1.3) and Play Families rules.
Secrets in the keystore or keychain, never in the bundle; certificate pinning where MASVS requires; no sensitive data in logs or screenshots.

The SDK inventory is a file beside the lockfiles (SDK, version, data collected, tracking). Tracking waits for the ATT grant and, in the EU, for consent (ePrivacy Art. 5(3), `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`). Personal data sent to a third party, third-party AI included, is disclosed and consented first (5.1.2(i)).
No hidden or dormant feature (2.3.1(a)). No downloaded code that changes features (2.5.2). A web wrapper fails 4.2, a near-copy 4.3.
Offline, background, interruption, and low-battery states tested on the lowest and newest OS.

Budgets on the lowest supported device: cold start, frame time, memory, and size (Macrobenchmark, XCTest launch metrics). Crash and ANR rates stay under Play's thresholds, and memory too from February 2027; hangs show in Xcode Organizer.
The MASVS controls, MASWE weaknesses, and MASTG cases for the change's category.
Notes for Review name each new feature (2.3.1(a)) and give a working demo account or demo mode, back end on (2.1(a)).
A new personal Play account runs a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days first; the pre-launch report is read before promotion.
App Store phased release or a Play staged rollout, halted on the crash-free or ANR trigger. A shipped binary cannot be recalled, so a server-side switch is the rollback.

name: Desktop apps
signal: macOS, Windows, and Linux apps, Electron, Tauri, their signing, updater, and stores

scope.not_when: the change is a command-line tool or library with no installer, or a web app in a browser tab, which `aidd-team:web-front-end` covers

standards.as: WCAG 2.2 for desktop software, applied through WCAG2ICT

obligations.what: A public code-signing certificate issued from this date lasts at most 460 days. Renew it yearly, and timestamp each signature so it outlives the certificate.
CRA (EU): report an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident on the clocks in `aidd-team:incident-response`, older products included. The main obligations apply from 2027-12-11.
Microsoft Store Policies 7.20 take effect.
EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: software placed on the market after this date is a product, and a missing security update can make it defective.

checklist.item: For a change to signing, entitlements, the updater, the installer, or a store listing, the author declares the security dimension (major). The release channel's rules are a dependency. A commercial app on the EU market is in CRA scope, and, once placed after 2026-12-09, in the Product Liability Directive's.
Each channel named with its signing and update path (`references/distribution.md`). A Mac App Store build is sandboxed, updates only through the store, and has no license screen (2.4.5).

Electron: context isolation and the sandbox on, and Node integration off in every renderer. A CSP; navigation, new windows, and IPC senders checked; no remote code; fuses flipped at package time. An Electron major inside its support window, the latest three.
Tauri: the fewest capabilities per window, a CSP, and the isolation pattern where the front end runs code it did not write.

Updates signed and verified before install (the Tauri updater's signature, Electron's updater on a signed build). The update key outside the repository. No downloaded code that changes described features (Store 10.2.2), and a Store game updates only through the Store (10.2.5).
Each entitlement and hardened runtime exception has a reason in the Spec; none disables library validation without one.
The UI meets WCAG 2.2 AA through WCAG2ICT, and works with each platform's screen reader (VoiceOver, Narrator, Orca).
macOS: Developer ID signed, hardened runtime, notarized, ticket stapled to the app, DMG, or PKG. Windows: every PE file signed and timestamped, chained to the Microsoft Trusted Root Program.

name: AI features
signal: a model call, retrieval, embeddings, or fine-tuning

scope.not_when: no model, retrieval, or embedding runs when the product does

standards.as: NIST AI RMF and NIST AI 600-1
Token and GPU cost as a FinOps unit metric

obligations.what: Article 50 applies: people know they deal with an AI system, and generated content is marked.
Article 50(2): a generative system on the market before 2026-08-02 marks its output. AI systems that generate non-consensual sexual deepfakes or child sexual abuse material are prohibited.
California: a business that uses automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) for a significant decision meets the CPPA's rules.
Colorado SB26-189: an ADMT developer documents it for deployers, and a deployer gives notice, explains an adverse outcome within 30 days, and offers human review.
The rules for high-risk AI systems in Annex III apply.
The rules for high-risk AI embedded in products regulated under Annex I apply.

checklist.item: Classify the feature by EU AI Act tier and NIST AI RMF risk. A prohibited use stops; a high-risk use is major, with the compliance analyst. A model that guides a decision on a person's job, housing, credit, insurance, care, or schooling is ADMT in California and Colorado.
Golden dataset, eval thresholds, and a regression eval per kept behavior, in the Acceptance.
Model, prompt, and parameters pinned in the Spec; a documentation Task updates the model card.

Model output is untrusted input: validate structured output once complete, bound latency, guard against prompt injection (LLM01) and data leakage (LLM02). Caps in layers stop the calls (LLM06): max tokens per call, a budget per user that counts partial output, and the provider's spend limit. A stream stops its model call when the user stops, runs a tool call once its input validates in full, and bounds its buffer.
Generated media carries a machine-readable mark (C2PA Content Credentials or a watermark); a deepfake says so (Art. 50).
Evals ran on head against the thresholds; failure modes and human oversight documented.
Canary with eval and cost rollback triggers; prompts and outputs logged under the privacy rules.

open_choices.question: Does a gateway sit between the code and the model providers?
open_choices.default: No gateway for one provider: one module calls its SDK and sets max_tokens, a timeout, and bounded retries. Add a gateway when the product needs two providers, a fallback, or shared spend caps.

open_choices.question: Where are the caps on model spending enforced?
open_choices.default: In the one module that calls the model, through the provider's SDK, with the provider's own spend limit behind it. A gateway's budgets per key take over once the project runs a gateway.
options: the provider's SDK in the calling module

open_choices.question: Where are the embeddings stored and searched?
open_choices.default: pgvector in the PostgreSQL database the application already runs, until the corpus or the query load needs a dedicated vector database.

open_choices.question: Where does the model run?
open_choices.default: A hosted provider's API. Serve an open-weights model yourself only when data residency, cost at volume, or a model the providers do not offer asks for it: vLLM on GPUs behind the gateway, and Ollama on a developer's machine.

references.holds: the model registry, reproducible training, and drift

name: AI agents and tools
signal: an agent, tool calling, MCP, or A2A

scope.not_when: a model answers but calls no tool and takes no action

standards.as: MCP and A2A, with the MCP security best practices

checklist.item: A new tool, MCP server, or permission is major: name the irreversible actions it can take.
Least privilege per tool: an allow-list of actions, scopes, and hosts; human approval for irreversible actions, showing the exact tool, arguments, and target (ASI09); a kill switch.
Trust boundaries drawn: what the agent reads is untrusted, what it may do is a tool (OWASP Agentic ASI01, ASI02).
An agent that reads untrusted input and holds tools uses plan-then-execute, with the plan fixed before the input arrives, or a dual-LLM split, where a quarantined model with no tools reads it.

Each agent acts under its own identity with short-lived, scoped delegated tokens, never a person's full token or a shared key (ASI03). An agent-to-agent call authenticates both ends and treats the reply as untrusted (ASI07).
Sandbox tool execution; validate tool arguments against schemas; no secret in the agent's context; every tool call traced with the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions.
MCP tool pinning: hash each tool's reviewed definition (name, description, input and output schemas, annotations). A changed hash fails closed, so the tool stays off until a person reviews it.
Agent memory records each entry's source, is scoped to one user or tenant, expires, and holds no secret. Untrusted text is never stored as an instruction (ASI06).
Trace an injected instruction from each input to each tool and show it is blocked or waits for a human.
Tool-call error rate, unusual action volume, and cost are the observe signals; a spike rolls back.

name: Data and analytics
signal: pipelines, warehouses, schemas, ML data

scope.not_when: the change touches one service's own tables with no schema, contract, or pipeline change

checklist.item: A schema, contract, or pipeline change names its producers and consumers; a migration is major (`baseline:migrations`).
The data contract change (ODCS) is written before Spec approval and listed in `design.files`; quality rules (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness) as tests.
A shared data product has an ODPS descriptor: an owner and an ODCS contract per output port.

Search: the database's own full-text search first (PostgreSQL `tsvector` with a GIN index), a search engine only for a measured need. The index follows the data by outbox or change data capture, per-tenant queries filter by tenant, and judged queries prove relevance.

Training data is a pinned, versioned snapshot, and each run and eval records its model and data snapshot in the model registry. A model and its datasets get a model card and a CycloneDX ML-BOM entry (`aidd-team:ai-features`).
Idempotent, restartable jobs, with the delivery guarantee stated against the transport's own; lineage emitted (OpenLineage); no personal data in fixtures or logs.
Warehouse personal data is classified in the contract and masked by column; each reader role sees only the columns it needs.
Lineage names each consumer of a changed field; a breaking contract change waits for them or keeps the old version to a stated date.
Row counts, freshness, and null rates are the observe signals; consumers are notified. For a model, input, prediction, and outcome drift too, wired to the rollback trigger.

tests.proves: producers and consumers pass the contract
tests.how: `uvx --from datacontract-cli==1.2.2 datacontract test datacontract.yaml` in CI

tests.name: Data product descriptor check
tests.proves: the ODPS descriptor validates
tests.how: `uvx check-jsonschema==0.38.2` with the ODPS v1.1.0 schema

name: Payments and finance

terms.meaning: An authorization holds the funds; a capture takes them. An uncaptured authorization expires.
A void cancels before settlement, a refund returns money after it, and a chargeback is the issuer's reversal.
The day the money moves between banks, days after the authorization.
An amount as an integer in the currency's smallest unit: JPY has no decimals, KWD has three.
The party that sells, and answers for tax, refunds, and disputes.

invariants.holds: Debits equal credits for every ledger entry.
invariants.missed: A fee, a partial refund, or a currency conversion posted on one side only.

invariants.holds: A refund never exceeds what was captured, less earlier refunds.
invariants.missed: Two concurrent partial refunds, or a refund on a charge already disputed.

invariants.holds: Money moves once per idempotency key.
invariants.missed: A webhook delivered twice, or a timed-out request retried after the PSP succeeded.

invariants.holds: A settled payment is never voided.
invariants.missed: A "cancel" on an order paid last week, which must be a refund.

signal: card data, ledgers, money movement

scope.not_when: the product only redirects to a hosted checkout and stores no payment state; an embedded payment form is in scope

obligations.what: Verification of Payee: a euro-area payment service provider checks the payee's name against the account before a credit transfer, and the rest of the EU by 2027-07-09.
CCD2 applies to new EU consumer credit, buy now, pay later and loans below EUR 200 included.
The EU AML Regulation applies to obliged entities, crypto-asset service providers among them.

checklist.item: Card data, ledgers, or money movement: the financial dimension, major, the finance pool. A PCI scope change is its own decision. An EU financial entity also answers to DORA.
Double-entry invariants and idempotency for every money movement in the Acceptance; reconciliation and the audit trail named.

An EEA card payment names its SCA path: EMV 3DS 2 with the data for a frictionless result. It names each exemption claimed (low value, transaction risk analysis, merchant-initiated, recurring) and by whom. It names what a challenge or a failure does to the payment.

Credit names its disclosures, its creditworthiness assessment, the human review an automated decision allows, and its adverse action reasons. A crypto-asset service names its MiCA authorisation. `references/credit-crypto-and-aml.md` holds the detail.

Onboarding and payouts screen every payer and payee against the sanctions lists before money moves, with KYC by risk. A crypto-asset transfer carries the travel rule's originator and beneficiary data.

No card data stored, logged, or in fixtures outside the PCI scope. The PSP's token or a network token stands in for the PAN, with its lifecycle updates handled. Amounts as integers in minor units with a currency; timestamps with an explicit zone.

Payment pages: every script inventoried with its reason and integrity check (PCI DSS 6.4.3). Payment pages also have a change- and tamper-detection mechanism that alerts on script and header changes (11.6.1).
A subscription shows its renewal terms before the first charge and stops as easily as it started (EU withdrawal function; US ROSCA and auto-renewal laws).
Every payment state transition is idempotent and replay-safe; failure paths reconcile; the PSP's webhooks are verified and deduplicated before they move the ledger.

Disputes and chargebacks: each has its own states and ledger entries. The evidence a dispute needs (the 3DS result, delivery, the customer's consent) is retrievable, and the response deadline is tracked.
The reconciliation report is clean for the observe window; a rollback preserves the ledger with compensating entries, never deletes.

name: Commerce and marketplaces

terms.meaning: A marketplace hosts other sellers' offers; the merchant of record sells.
A seller acting for business purposes, whom a marketplace must trace under the DSA.
A SKU is one product variant; a listing is one seller's offer of it.
Stock set aside for a cart or an order, released when it expires.
The goods coming back, and the money going back: either can happen without the other.
A review written in exchange for something of value, which must say so.
A marketplace the tax law treats as the seller, so it charges and pays the VAT (EU).

invariants.holds: Stock never goes below zero across concurrent checkouts.
invariants.missed: Two carts buying the last unit, or a hold that expired but was never released.

invariants.holds: An order's total equals its lines, discounts, tax, and shipping, in one currency.
invariants.missed: A coupon applied again after a partial refund or a split shipment.

invariants.holds: A review is shown only when a real customer wrote it, marked when incentivised.
invariants.missed: A seller's staff posting reviews, or negative reviews suppressed.

invariants.holds: A seller is verified before it sells, and again when its details change.
invariants.missed: A seller changing its bank account after verification.

invariants.holds: The first price shown is the total the buyer pays, mandatory fees included.
invariants.missed: A service fee added at the last step, against US fee rules for tickets and lodging.

scope.not_when: the product sells nothing and hosts no other seller

obligations.what: The INFORM Consumers Act applies: a US marketplace collects, verifies, and discloses its high-volume third-party sellers' details.
The FTC rule on consumer reviews and testimonials is in effect: no fake, bought, or insider reviews, and no review suppression.
The GPSR applies: an EU marketplace registers on Safety Gate, names a single point of contact, and acts on recalls and takedown orders.
US: the FTC fees rule applies to live-event tickets and short-term lodging: the total price, mandatory fees included, shows first.
The European Accessibility Act applies to e-commerce services sold to consumers in the EU.
EU: an online contract with a right of withdrawal offers the withdrawal function.

checklist.item: A marketplace with other sellers: trader traceability, product safety, and seller verification are in scope. Name the markets the change serves.
The order's states and transitions in one state machine, with the stock hold and its expiry; every total named in minor units with its currency.

A seller's identity, bank, and contact details are verified before its first sale and again on a change; the traders' details are shown to buyers. A change to sellers' terms gives at least 15 days' notice, and a restriction gives its reasons (EU P2B).
Name who charges and pays VAT or sales tax in each market: the marketplace as deemed supplier (EU) or marketplace facilitator (US states), or the seller.

Reviews come only from verified orders or say why not; an incentivised review is marked; no review is hidden for its rating. The first price shown is the total, mandatory fees included (US fee rules).
A recall or a takedown order removes the listing and notifies its buyers; the checkout meets the accessibility law of each market.
EU: a price cut names the lowest price of the prior 30 days; a review page says whether and how reviews are checked; search results state their main ranking parameters.
EU: an online contract with a withdrawal right offers a withdrawal function ('withdraw from contract here') for the whole withdrawal period, then 'confirm withdrawal' and an acknowledgement.
Concurrent checkouts of the last unit, an expired hold, and a refund after a split shipment each have a test.
Oversell, stuck orders, and refund failures are rollback triggers; the reconciliation of orders, payments, and stock is the observe signal.

The provider or plan, and the vendor that handles PHI for it under a business associate agreement (US, HIPAA).
Use and disclose only the PHI the purpose needs (US, HIPAA).
A FHIR resource is the base type (Patient); a profile such as US Core constrains it.
A practice that interferes with access to electronic health information, unless an exception applies (US, ONC).

invariants.missed: A batch export, a support user's impersonation, or a cached report.

invariants.holds: A patient's access to their own records is never blocked or slowed.
invariants.missed: A rate limit or a manual review on the patient-facing API.

invariants.holds: Clinical data is amended, never silently changed.
invariants.missed: Merging duplicate patient records without the history of each.

invariants.holds: A value keeps its unit and its code (UCUM, LOINC, SNOMED CT).

Name whether the software is a medical device by its intended use (FDA's CDS and general wellness guidances in the US; MDR Rule 11 and MDCG 2019-11 in the EU), and its class.

A certified API or a patient's access request is never blocked or slowed without an information blocking exception, recorded (45 CFR Part 171).
PHI encrypted in transit and at rest; an audit log for every access; no PHI in logs, fixtures, or prompts. A US health app outside HIPAA reports a breach under the FTC rule.
Device software: the IEC 81001-5-1 activities (threat model, secure coding, security tests). For a cyber device, also an SBOM per release and a vulnerability monitoring and disclosure plan (524B).

The hazard analysis (ISO 14971) is updated for the change; requirements trace to tests.
Assurance follows the intended use's risk (CSA): scripted tests where a failure harms quality or safety, unscripted ones elsewhere; device software's records meet the QMSR.
Patient-facing pages and apps meet WCAG 2.1 AA where Section 504 or the ADA reaches (US), and the EAA's standard in the EU.

name: Products for children

terms.meaning: Under 13 for COPPA; under the digital-consent age in the EU, 13 to 16 by member state; under 18 for the UK Children's Code and the DSA.
Consent by a method reasonably calculated to make sure it is the parent who gives it.
Knowing a user is a child, which brings COPPA's duties to a general-audience service.
Age estimation or verification, in proportion to the risk.
A child's settings start at their most private.

invariants.holds: No personal data from a child before consent, unless an exception applies.
invariants.missed: An analytics or crash SDK that sends a device id at first launch.

invariants.holds: A child's new feature starts at its most private setting.
invariants.missed: A feature shipped with sharing or location on.

invariants.holds: A child's data is kept only as long as its purpose needs, by a written policy.
invariants.missed: Backups, logs, and the vendor's copy.

checklist.item: Users under 13, minors in the EU, or a UK service likely to be accessed by children: the privacy and compliance dimensions, major, the privacy pool.
Age assurance, verifiable parental consent, data minimization, and defaults (private by default, no profiling, no nudges) in the Acceptance.

The age assurance method is chosen by risk (verification, estimation, or inference, stepped up where the harm is high), with its error rates. A neutral age screen sets no default age and gives no hint of the cut-off. Its fallback is never a dead end. Where a US state or national law requires it, the app reads the store's or the operating system's age signal, and the team checks each law's date at source.

A service that minors in Brazil use has age verification and parental supervision tools, and no ad profiling (ECA Digital). An Australian social media platform keeps under-16s from holding an account.

No behavioral advertising, no geolocation by default, no dark pattern; plain-language notices; separate verifiable parental consent before any disclosure to third parties, targeted advertising included. A parent can review and delete their child's data and withdraw consent.
Every flow of a child's data has a lawful basis and a retention limit that the published data retention policy states. The information security program covers the change.

A student who is 18 or in postsecondary education: the FERPA rights pass to them (US, FERPA).
Data a school may disclose unless the parent or student opted out (US, FERPA).
The classes, enrolments, and people a school's system sends (OneRoster).
A signed message by which a learning platform starts a tool in the user's context.

invariants.missed: A vendor reusing records to build its own product or to target ads.

invariants.missed: A timed quiz with no way to grant extra time.

ADA Title II: a public entity of 50,000 or more, a public school district or university among them, meets WCAG 2.1 AA on the web and in apps.
EU AI Act: an AI system that decides admission, assesses learning, steers education, or detects cheating in tests is high-risk (Annex III).
ADA Title II: a public entity under 50,000, or a special district, meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

In the EU and UK: the GDPR, with the school as controller. A child under the market's age of digital consent: `aidd-team:products-for-children` too.
Each disclosure of a record names its FERPA basis; directory information honors each opt-out; a parent's or eligible student's access request is served.
An AI feature that scores, admits, or proctors names its Annex III status, its human review, and its evaluation by group. No AI system infers a student's emotions (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f)).
Launch and grade passback through LTI 1.3 with its security framework; rostering through OneRoster 1.2, deprovisioning included.
A grade or credit change records who, when, and why, and keeps the earlier value.
A badge or a transcript is issued as a signed, verifiable credential (Open Badges 3.0, CLR 2.0) that can be revoked.
Every learner-facing screen meets WCAG 2.2 AA, which covers the WCAG 2.1 AA the ADA rule names; a timed assessment allows extra time.

name: HR and workforce

terms.meaning: Three kinds of person, with different laws, data, and retention.
An automated employment decision tool, which NYC Local Law 144 requires a yearly bias audit for.
A group's selection rate below four-fifths of the highest group's rate, the US Uniform Guidelines' rule of thumb.
The day a change to pay, role, or manager takes effect, which can differ from the day it was entered.
The starting pay or range of a job. The EU directive makes an employer give it before the interview, and many US states require it in the posting.

invariants.holds: A pay record adds up and is kept for its legal period.
invariants.missed: A retroactive raise, or a termination before payday.

invariants.holds: A screening or ranking tool is tested for adverse impact before use and on a schedule.
invariants.missed: A model update after the last audit.

invariants.holds: A person sees only the people data they may see.
invariants.missed: A manager's view of a peer's salary, or an export to a shared drive.

invariants.holds: A change takes effect on its effective date.
invariants.missed: A future-dated promotion applied today, or a backdated pay change that skips payroll.

signal: candidates, employees, pay, or hiring decisions

scope.not_when: the product holds no data about candidates or workers and makes no decision about them

obligations.what: NYC Local Law 144 is enforced: a bias audit within a year of use, its summary published, and notice to candidates and employees.
EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f): no AI system infers the emotions of a worker or a candidate at work, except for medical or safety reasons.
The EU Pay Transparency Directive's transposition deadline: pay ranges before the interview, no pay-history question, and pay-gap reporting.

EU Platform Work Directive transposition: a digital labour platform tells workers about its automated monitoring and decisions, has a person review them, and processes no emotional state or private conversation.
California: an employer that uses ADMT to make a significant decision about a candidate or a worker meets the CPPA's ADMT rules.

Colorado SB26-189: an ADMT that materially influences an employment decision is covered. Its developer gives deployers technical documentation; the deployer gives notice, an explanation within 30 days of an adverse outcome, and human review on request.
EU AI Act: an AI system for recruitment, selection, promotion, termination, task allocation, or monitoring of workers is high-risk (Annex III).

checklist.item: Candidate and employee data is privacy; a tool that ranks, screens, or decides about people is also an AI feature at high risk, and ADMT under California's and Colorado's rules. Name the countries and cities served, because Illinois and others add their own notice rules.

A selection tool names its adverse-impact test (selection rates by group, the four-fifths rule), its bias audit, its notice, how a candidate asks for an accommodation or an alternative, and the person who decides.
A job posting carries its pay range where the EU directive or a US state or city law requires it. No form asks for pay history, and pay data can report the gap by sex for each category of workers.

Before a monitoring or decision tool goes live, workers and their representatives are told (AI Act Art. 26(7)). A digital labour platform also keeps to the Platform Work Directive's limits, and no tool reads a worker's emotions.
Voluntary self-identification data is stored apart and never reaches the screener or a model's features. A criminal-history question waits for the stage the local fair-chance law allows.
Pay, role, and manager changes are effective-dated records with their approver. Payroll records are kept for their legal period, 3 years under the FLSA in the US, and time cards 2.
Working time is recorded each day where the law requires it. Tax tables, minimum wages, and overtime rules are data with their effective date and source, never constants in code.
Access to pay and performance data follows the reporting line and the purpose; exports are logged.
A model or rule change to a selection tool waits for a new adverse-impact result; payroll runs are reconciled before the first pay date.

name: Privacy by default
signal: personal data: user, customer, account, member, patient, or contact records, consent, data-subject requests, or a `gdpr` target in `project.compliance.targets`

scope.not_when: the change touches no field, store, log, or call that holds personal data

standards.as: GDPR, by the article each row names
CCPA/CPRA, the comparable US regime: notice at collection, and the rights to know, delete, correct, and opt out
LINDDUN over the threat model's data-flow diagram, for the risks to people

checklist.item: Personal data in the diff (the gate's personal-data baseline, or an added auth library), or `gdpr` in `project.compliance.targets`: the privacy dimension, major, the privacy pool, and the compliance analyst starts.
The Spec names every privacy regime the product serves, such as the UK GDPR as amended in 2025, US state laws, Brazil's LGPD, and India's DPDP Act. Build each right once, and map it to each regime.
An Initiative that collects a new category of personal data funds the data map, the rights endpoints, and the DPIA as work, not as Review-time fixes (Art. 25).

Each new or changed item gets its row in the one data map (`aidd new data-map`), whose columns are the records of processing (Art. 30). Classify every field as public, internal, personal, or special category, and collect only what the purpose needs (Art. 5(1)(c)). A DPIA trigger (Art. 35) means the DPIA is written before Spec approval.

Acceptance names each data-subject right the change touches. Each is answered within one month (Art. 12(3)), or 45 days under the CCPA. The rights are access and export (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction (Art. 18), portability (Art. 20), and objection (Art. 21); CCPA/CPRA adds know, delete, correct, and opt out. Endpoints and tests: `references/rights-and-records.md`.

Where consent is the lawful basis, it is specific, recorded with its version and time, and as easy to withdraw as to give (Art. 7). Storing or reading on a device needs consent unless strictly necessary (ePrivacy Art. 5(3)). Every purpose has a lawful basis (Art. 6), and the notice (Art. 13 and 14) changes with the data map.
A new processor gets its Art. 28 contract and a row in the data map's register. Data leaving the EEA names its mechanism (adequacy, SCCs, or BCRs, Art. 44-49) and its transfer impact assessment.

The retention schedule runs as code: each data-map row's retention is a scheduled deletion job (hard delete, anonymisation, or crypto-shredding). Backups expire within the stated period or are crypto-shredded.

Private by default (Art. 25(2)): optional processing off until chosen. No personal data in logs, URLs, analytics events, error reports, fixtures, seeds, snapshots, or a lower environment. Pseudonymise where the purpose allows.

Trace each new field, store, log line, and outbound call to its data-map row. A store missing from the map, a purpose without a lawful basis, or personal data in a log is a finding. The LINDDUN pass names the linking, identifying, and disclosure threats and their controls (Art. 32).

The breach runbook names who assesses a personal-data breach and starts the clocks (Art. 33 and 34) that `aidd-team:incident-response` lists. Rights-request volumes and deletion-job failures are observe signals.

tests.name: Erase request test
tests.proves: an erasure request removes the subject from every store the data map lists. The backup policy expires or crypto-shreds the rest within the stated period
tests.how: an integration test that seeds one subject in every mapped store, calls the erase endpoint, and asserts each store returns nothing for them. The test asserts the backup expiry from the backup config

tests.name: Export completeness test
tests.proves: an access or portability export returns every field the data map lists for the subject, in a structured, machine-readable format
tests.how: an API test that seeds a subject with every mapped field and compares the export's fields with the data map's rows

tests.name: Rectify and restrict test

tests.how: API tests over the rectify, restrict, and object endpoints, asserting the downstream jobs skip that subject

tests.name: Consent gate test
tests.proves: nothing optional is collected or shared before consent, and withdrawing consent stops it
tests.how: end-to-end tests with consent refused, given, and withdrawn, asserting the stored fields and the outbound calls

tests.name: Retention job test
tests.proves: records past their retention are deleted or anonymised by the scheduled job
tests.how: a unit test over the deletion job with a fixed clock

tests.name: Data map check
tests.proves: every data-map row names a purpose, a lawful basis, a retention, and a deletion method, and every column the classifier marks personal has a row
tests.how: a schema check over the data map in CI, joined with an automated PII scan of the database schema

tests.name: Masked test data check
tests.proves: no fixture, seed, or snapshot holds production personal data
tests.how: a PII scan (`presidio-analyzer` 2.2.364) over the test fixtures and seeds in CI

name: Internationalization
signal: more than one language or region

scope.not_when: the product ships one language to one region, and the i18n-ready default covers it

checklist.item: A change that adds or reorders user-visible text, or formats dates, numbers, or names, touches every locale. A market's language law, such as Quebec's Charter of the French Language, can make a locale required.
The locales in the Acceptance; text expansion, right-to-left, and pluralization cases named; the CLDR version the runtime ships, pinned.
A currency amount carries its ISO 4217 code and shows in the locale's format. Its storage in minor units is `aidd-team:payments-and-finance`'s.
No concatenated strings; ICU MessageFormat for plurals and gender (MessageFormat 2 only where the runtime's is stable); locale-aware formatting from CLDR; UTF-8 end to end.

Instants are stored in UTC. A future event at a local wall-clock time is stored as that local time plus its IANA zone id, so a rule change does not move it. The tz data comes from a pinned, updated source, never a hand-kept offset table.
Text is compared after Unicode normalization (NFC), sorted with the locale's collation, and cut at grapheme boundaries. Case changes use the locale, as the Turkish dotless i needs.

No hard-coded locale, time zone, or encoding. User-supplied text is isolated (`dir=auto`, `<bdi>`, or FSI and PDI), so the bidi algorithm does not reorder what surrounds it. Pseudo-localization passes.
Translation coverage per locale tracked; a missing string falls back visibly, never silently.

name: Multi-tenant SaaS
signal: code that reads or writes data belonging to a tenant, organization, workspace, or customer account in a shared deployment

scope.not_when: each customer runs its own deployment and database

standards.as: OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization, applied across tenants
SaaS tenant isolation guidance (AWS Well-Architected SaaS Lens; Azure's multitenant architecture guide agrees): isolation, noisy neighbours, and tenant cost

obligations.what: EU Data Act Art. 29: no switching charge, data egress included. Until then, a charge is at most the direct cost of the switch.

checklist.item: Name every table, bucket, cache key, queue, and search index the change touches that holds tenant data. A new one without a tenant key is a design question before Specify.
Where tenants hold their own keys, each tenant's data is encrypted under its key. A key the tenant revokes makes its data unreadable, and offboarding destroys the key.

Acceptance states that a client of tenant B cannot read, list, update, or delete tenant A's data through each changed operation. It names the expected response (404, not 403, where existence must not leak).
Every cross-tenant query (billing roll-ups, support tools, analytics) is named in the Spec. It runs under a separate role or service and is unreachable from customer-facing endpoints.

Each tenant-facing operation has a per-tenant quota or rate limit by tier (requests, storage, jobs), so one tenant cannot starve the rest. The Spec names the limit and the answer past it (429 with Retry-After).

Offboarding: a tenant's data can be exported in a documented format, then deleted from every store within a stated period. The stores: tables, replicas, caches, search, and object storage; backups as they expire. Switching under the EU Data Act: a notice period of at most two months, a transition of at most 30 days, and every exportable data and digital asset exported.
The tenant id comes only from the authenticated token or session. It never comes from the request body, the query string, a path parameter, or a header the client sets.
Tenant scoping lives in the data-access layer, in a base query or repository that every read and write goes through. A check after fetching the row is a finding, not a control.

Every joined or sub-queried table is filtered by the tenant id again. Cache keys, object-storage paths, search queries, queued jobs, events, and log lines carry the tenant id, and a worker sets the tenant context before its first query.
Row-level security (or the database's equivalent) enforces the same scoping as a second layer, with the application connecting under a role that cannot bypass it.
Trace each changed query to its tenant filter. Any raw query, bulk job, or new join without one, and any tenant id read from client input, is a finding.

A user in many tenants holds a token for one active tenant, and switching clears the client's cached data. Support access to a tenant's data is time-bound, granted where the contract says, and logged.
Cross-tenant access denials and any query that runs without a tenant context are logged and alerted on during the observe window.
Cost per tenant is measured (tags, metering, or usage attribution) and reported by tier as unit economics. A tier whose cost per tenant exceeds its price is a Learn action.

tests.name: Cross-tenant read test per data-access method
tests.proves: client B cannot see, list, or change client A's records through any repository method or endpoint the change touches
tests.how: a parameterized test that seeds two tenants and calls every data-access method and endpoint as tenant B against tenant A's ids, in the repository suite

tests.name: Tenant id from client input is ignored
tests.proves: a tenant id placed in the body, query, path, or a header does not change which tenant's data is returned
tests.how: API tests that send tenant A's id in each position with tenant B's token and assert tenant B's scope

tests.name: Row-level security enforced
tests.proves: the database refuses cross-tenant rows even when the application filter is missing
tests.how: on PostgreSQL, a test connects as the application role, sets tenant A's context, and runs an unfiltered `SELECT` on each tenant table, expecting only A's rows. It checks that a pooled connection reused after a transaction carries no tenant, and a migration test checks `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. On another database, the same test runs against its row-level security

tests.name: Unscoped query lint
tests.proves: no query on a tenant table bypasses the scoped base query
tests.how: a Semgrep rule (`uvx semgrep==1.180.0`), or the ORM's own check, that flags raw queries and direct model access on tenant tables outside the data-access layer

tests.name: Per-tenant quota enforced
tests.proves: a tenant past its limit gets 429 with Retry-After while another tenant's requests still succeed
tests.how: a load test with one scenario per tenant, in the runner `apis-and-services:load-test` names (default k6). It drives tenant A past its tier's limit and asserts that tenant B's success rate and p95 hold

tests.name: Tenant offboarding export and delete
tests.proves: a tenant's export holds all its records, and after deletion no store returns any of them

signal: a package or formula published to a public registry

obligations.what: CRA reporting applies to a manufacturer (Art. 14), for a package placed on the market earlier too (`aidd-team:incident-response`).

checklist.item: The release workflow is a CI/CD protected path (major, the security pool). A first publish names the package, the namespace, and the owner accounts in the Spec, and every owner account has phishing-resistant 2FA.
The version bump follows the public API diff, not the commit messages alone; a major bump names its migration note.
The registry's own rules are Acceptance: Maven Central's sources and javadoc jars, `.asc` signatures, and POM metadata; Homebrew's stable tagged release built from source.

Publish only from CI by trusted publishing (OIDC). The publish job alone gets the OIDC token, as `id-token: write` on GitHub Actions or `id_tokens:` on GitLab CI, and no registry token sits in secrets. Disable token publishing where the registry allows it.
Provenance goes out with the artifact: npm provenance, PyPI attestations (PEP 740), or a GitHub artifact attestation, built from a public repository.

A LICENSE matching the manifest's SPDX identifier, a SECURITY.md with contacts, and a contribution guide (OSPS Baseline level 1). Under the CRA, SECURITY.md is the steward's or the manufacturer's vulnerability policy.

Governance: GOVERNANCE.md names the maintainers, their roles, and how decisions and releases are made; CODEOWNERS asks an owner to review release and security paths; each commit carries a DCO sign-off where the project takes outside contributions.
The dry run's file list holds no secret, fixture, or build leftover, and the API report's diff matches the bump.
Scorecard shows no drop since the last release in Token-Permissions, Pinned-Dependencies, Signed-Releases, Branch-Protection, or Security-Policy.

Publish from the tag, with an SBOM (CycloneDX or SPDX) beside the artifact. Verify the published artifact's provenance from the registry, and keep the previous version installable. A bad release is deprecated or yanked, never overwritten.
Turn on immutable releases and staged publishing where the release host and the registry offer them. A product sold under the CRA states its support period.

terms.meaning: An in-game currency bought with real money, whose real cost must stay clear.
A loot box: an item of random content bought with money or virtual currency.

The right to an item or currency that a store receipt grants, once.
IARC's, PEGI's, ESRB's, or a national body's rating, given for content and for features such as purchases and chat.

invariants.holds: Currency and inventory change only on the server, once per receipt or event.
invariants.missed: A client-reported reward, or a receipt replayed after a refund.

invariants.holds: A refund or a chargeback takes back what it granted.
invariants.missed: A refunded currency pack already spent on items.

invariants.holds: A save is never lost or half-written.
invariants.missed: A crash during a save, or two devices syncing one save.

invariants.holds: A paid random item never reaches a player the rating or the law excludes.
invariants.missed: A minor in Brazil, where loot boxes in games children are likely to play are banned.

obligations.what: The DSA applies to a game that hosts player content: a notice-and-action path, and a statement of reasons for each decision.
UK Online Safety Act: Ofcom enforces the illegal content duties of a game where players chat or share content.
The CPC Network's key principles on virtual currencies guide EU enforcement: clear prices, no hidden costs, the right of withdrawal, and care for children.

checklist.item: Name the markets, the platforms, and the age rating; a game minors are likely to play also loads `aidd-team:products-for-children`. Console certification (Sony's TRC, Microsoft's XR, Nintendo's Lotcheck) is under NDA, so the team's own checklist holds it.
The economy is server-authoritative: currency, inventory, and outcomes change only on the server; each purchase is granted once by its receipt and taken back on a refund.

Virtual currency shows its real-money cost; a paid random item shows its odds, rates PEGI 16 or 18, and is off for minors in Brazil. Currency delivered at once needs the player's express consent and acknowledgement that the 14-day withdrawal right ends (EU).

Player content (chat, names, uploads) has a notice-and-action path: a report, a decision with its statement of reasons, and an appeal where the game is an online platform. Chat can be blocked and muted. UK players: the illegal content risk assessment.
Saves are atomic (write, then rename), versioned, and checksummed, with one rule for a sync conflict across devices.

Captions for speech and key sounds, resizable text, and remappable controls; the store and checkout meet WCAG 2.2 AA where the EAA applies. In-game text and voice chat are accessible where the US CVAA reaches.
No pressure in purchase flows: no false urgency, hidden cost, or appeal to children to buy. Design for the Digital Fairness Act proposal, but never claim it.
Currency created and spent, and grants per receipt, are the observe signals; an imbalance or a double grant is a rollback trigger.
